title: Audit log retention & pipeline ops notes
content:
Purpose

Operational notes for audit log storage, retention tiers, indexing pipeline and backfill strategies. This doc is an engineering + compliance working draft to capture failure modes, automation hooks for evidence collection, and SIEM export constraints. It assumes RBAC v2 for access control and the canonical audit schema (see linked artifacts).

High level retention policy (recommended)
- Hot index (OpenSearch): 0–90 days. Fast search, low-latency access for investigations and live dashboards.
- Warm/analytics store (BigQuery): 90 days–1 year. Reasonable query latency for cross-correlation and long-running investigations.
- Cold / legal archives (S3 with Object Lock): 1–7 years. Immutable, encrypted, holdable for legal holds/DSARs.
- Absolute deletion after 7 years unless legal hold or customer-specific retention override configured.

Key constraints and controls
- Encryption: TLS in transit, KMS-backed encryption at rest for S3/BigQuery/OpenSearch.
- Immutability: Use S3 Object Lock + Governance mode for legal hold windows when needed.
- Access: RBAC v2 enforced at ingestion, indexing, and archive read paths. No direct console access without just-in-time escalation (JIT).
- PII handling: Redaction pipeline stage before moving to BigQuery or SIEM unless an approved exception exists. Redaction logs are stored separately and treated as restricted evidence.

Pipeline architecture summary
- Producers (app services) -> Kafka topic (audit-raw) -> Stream processors (Cloud Run / Dataflow) -> Validation + Enrichment -> Two sinks: OpenSearch (hot), S3 raw events (cold). Periodic ETL -> BigQuery for analytics.
- SIEM export: Scheduled export job pulls from BigQuery nightly, transforms to SIEM schema, pushes to customer SIEM endpoints (syslog/HTTP). Exports include integrity checksum and tenant scoping metadata.

Indexing and backfill patterns
- Incremental indexing: consumers maintain per-partition offsets in ZooKeeper/State store. Use small batches (<10k events) and aggressive bulk API to OpenSearch to reduce overhead.
- Backfill from raw store: use Spark job that reads S3 raw with checkpointed offsets; rehydrate enrichment (use same enrichment version as production tag), write to temp index, run compare diff and swap alias to minimize downtime.
- Idempotence: every audit event must include stable event_id and source_offset. Indexer de-dups by event_id. Backfills should mark reindexed_range in metadata to prevent double-counting.

Failure modes and mitigations
- Consumer lag / Kafka backlog: alert when lag > threshold; scale consumers; if sustained, cut retention for hot index to free space and prioritize critical topics.
- Schema drift: validation stage rejects unknown fields and emits a rejected-event topic. Alert on >0.5% rejects in 1h window. Maintain schema registry and automated compatibility checks in CI.
- Partial writes to OpenSearch: implement two-phase write (write to temp doc then bulk commit); verify via checksum query; retry queue for failed batches.
- Corrupt messages in S3: raw objects include checksum header (SHA256). Repair process: attempt re-parse with tolerant parser, else mark object quarantined and notify security/compliance.
- Indexer OOM: set circuit-breaker; spill to disk; auto-restart with recent offset checkpoint; run backpressure by pausing producers via throttling.
- SIEM export failure: exports kept in a durable outgoing queue (S3) with retry/backoff and dead-letter bucket. For endpoint changes, apply feature-flagged export versions.

Automation for evidence collection and DSARs
- Evidence automation hooks: evidence-service subscribes to audit-raw-relevant events and creates a case bundle (logs, enrichment, metadata) in evidence-store. Bundles reference S3 URIs and index snapshots.
- DSAR/process: legal holds attach to tenant_id and prevent deletion. Deletions require a clearance ticket and compliance approval; runbook outlines steps for redaction vs deletion.

Operational telemetry and alerts
- KPIs: consumer lag, indexing throughput (docs/sec), bulk failure rate, S3 write error rate, backfill progress %, SIEM export success %.
- Dashboards: OpenSearch cluster health, BigQuery job queue, S3 archive size, legal hold count.
- Alerts: SLA breach (indexing lag > 30m), failed backfill job, checksum mismatch, >1% schema rejects.

Runbook excerpts (quick actions)
- Investigate indexing lag:
  1) Check Kafka consumer group offsets: kafka-consumer-groups --describe --group audit-indexers
  2) Check CPU/memory of indexers; scale replicas.
  3) Verify OpenSearch shard allocation: curl _cat/shards
  4) If time-critical: pause non-critical producers with throttle API.
- Recover from failed backfill:
  1) Identify batch id and S3 prefix.
  2) Re-run Spark job with --force-reindex and smaller chunk size.
  3) Validate sample events in temp index, then swap alias.
- SIEM export troubleshooting:
  1) Inspect last successful export file in s3://redwood-exports/siem-outgoing/
  2) Replay with export-tool --simulate --target <endpoint>
  3) If endpoint rejects: place files in dead-letter and open ticket with customer.

Open questions / follow-ups
- Retention tiers and legal minimums per geography (EU vs US) — need compliance confirmation for 7-year default.
- RBAC v2 mapping: who can trigger backfills or delete archived objects? Define roles and just-in-time approval flow.
- SIEM export PII allowances — define an allow list per customer and automation for per-customer transformations.

Appendix: short checklist before a major reindex/backfill
- Lock write alias, enable maintenance mode on index consumers.
- Snapshot current index and verify S3 canonical backup checksums.
- Run dry-run Spark job on subset and validate schema/enrichment parity.
- Notify stakeholders and open JIRA runbook ticket.

If this doc is used as the source of truth for runbooks, please raise to in_review and attach step-by-step playbook fragments as separate docs (playbooks should be shorter and prescriptive).
